subject: A single architectural grid-frame model: a lattice skeleton of thin pale timber members forming exactly 4 columns by 3 rows of square cells (like the frame of a hanok courtyard house or a display shelf grid), standing alone on a low dark plinth in a museum. Exactly one cell, lower left, holds a muted red panel.
purpose: Photo set inside the square counter of a huge Korean letter on a black magazine page; the whole object must fill a wide frame edge to edge.
style: Editorial museum photography, real photograph, sharp, medium-format look, no illustration. Same material and joinery as a refined timber model.
composition: Strictly frontal and orthographic, no perspective, the model's outer frame is a rectangle about 1.36:1, filling about 92% of the frame height and centred, even black margin, plinth just visible at the bottom, all edges of the model straight and parallel to the frame.
palette: Near-black background, warm pale wood, one muted red cell.
lighting: Single soft museum spotlight from above, deep shadows, no glare.
notes: Background must fall to pure black so it sits on a (4,5,5) black page. The whole model must be visible; no part cropped.
